title: Parking a Goods Vehicle
whatItIs: A goods vehicle over 7.5 tonnes must not be parked on a verge, pavement or land between carriageways without police permission. Park off-street where you can, and secure your vehicle.

keyFacts.text: Over 7.5 t (trailer included): you MUST NOT park on a verge, pavement or central land without police permission.
Only exception: parking there is essential for loading or unloading, and then the vehicle MUST NOT be left unattended.
Before leaving your vehicle you MUST switch off the engine, headlights and fog lights, and apply the handbrake.
You MUST NOT leave your vehicle or trailer in a dangerous position or where it causes unnecessary obstruction.
All vehicles MUST show parking lights when parked on a road or lay-by with a speed limit over 30 mph.

keyFacts: Use off-street parking areas or bays marked with white lines wherever possible.

items.title: Verges and pavements
items.text: Over 7.5 t: never without police permission, unless essential for loading.

items.title: At night
items.text: Goods vehicles over 2,500 kg laden MUST NOT be left on a road at night without lights.

items.title: Loading and unloading
items.text: Don't load or unload where yellow kerb markings and signs show restrictions.

items.title: Places to avoid
items.text: Within 10 m of a junction, on a bend, near a hill brow, a bus stop or a level crossing.

items.title: Security
items.text: Remove the key, close the windows, lock the vehicle and never leave vehicle documents inside.

items.title: Passing places
items.text: Don't park in passing places on single-track roads.

a.label: Goods vehicle over 7.5 t
points: MUST NOT park on verges or pavements without police permission
Loading there only if essential, and never unattended

b.label: Vehicle up to 7.5 t
points: The 7.5 t verge rule does not apply
Still should not park on pavements unless signs permit it

onTheTest.question: You drive an 18-tonne rigid lorry. When may you park it on a grass verge without police permission?
options: Only when essential for loading or unloading, and never unattended
Whenever there is no space on the road
Overnight, if you leave the lights on
At weekends, when traffic is light
onTheTest.why: Vehicles over 7.5 tonnes must not be parked on a verge without police permission. The only exception is when it is essential for loading or unloading, and then the vehicle must not be left unattended.

onTheTest.question: You leave your lorry parked on a road at night where the speed limit is 30 mph. What must you do?
options: Nothing, as the limit is 30 mph
Leave the hazard warning lights on
onTheTest.why: Only cars and goods vehicles up to 2,500 kg laden may park without lights on a 30 mph road. Other vehicles must not be left on a road at night without lights.

traps: The 7.5 t limit for verges and pavements includes any trailer.
Loading on a verge is allowed only if essential, and you MUST stay with the vehicle.
The 30 mph 'no lights at night' exemption is for goods vehicles up to 2,500 kg, not lorries.
Check for cyclists before you open your cab door: you MUST NOT hit anyone with it.

jurisdictionNotes.text: In Scotland you MUST NOT park partially or wholly on the pavement, or double park (limited exceptions).
In London you MUST NOT park partially or wholly on the pavement (limited exceptions).
